question: Which of the following complexes is also called a light-harvesting complex?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Antenna Complex**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• The **Antenna Complex**, also known as the **light-harvesting complex**, is a group of protein and pigment molecules found in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria. 
• It plays a crucial role in **photosynthesis** by capturing light energy from the sun and transferring it to the **reaction center chlorophyll molecules**. 
• The pigments in the antenna complex include **chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, and carotenoids**, which absorb light at different wavelengths to maximize energy capture. 
• These complexes are organized into photosystems, specifically **Photosystem I (PSI) and Photosystem II (PSII)**, each with distinct roles in the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.
